Use it for: Daily mandi prices, other open government datasets
Steps: 1) Register and get an API key. 2) Test the query in a browser/Postman. 3) Write a paginated fetch with retries. 4) Insert with a unique key (date, market, commodity, variety) to avoid duplicates. 5) Log row counts per day.
Pitfalls to avoid: Current-day only responses; rate limits; changing field names. Save raw JSON as backup.

Steps: 1) Download from the official page. 2) Keep the original file unchanged in /data/raw. 3) Clean into /data/processed with a script. 4) Record URL, date, licence in the sources table.
Pitfalls to avoid: Editing raw files by hand; losing track of the source and date.

Use it for: Guidelines, area/production statistics, groundwater and project reports
Steps: 1) Identify the pages with tables. 2) Extract with Camelot/pdfplumber. 3) Compare 5-10 values with the PDF by eye. 4) Fix merged cells and units. 5) Save the page number as a source reference.
Pitfalls to avoid: Scanned PDFs need OCR; units (quintal vs tonne, ha vs acre) differ between tables.

Use it for: Directories (cold storage, FSSAI units), vendor price listings
Steps: 1) Read the site's terms and robots.txt first. 2) Fetch politely (delay between requests). 3) Parse into rows. 4) Store the page URL and access date.
Pitfalls to avoid: Violating terms of use; fragile selectors; CAPTCHAs. Prefer APIs or manual collection if scraping is not allowed.

Tools: Overpass API, OSRM, Google Places (as in your plan), QGIS
Steps: 1) Write an Overpass query for the tags (e.g. cold storage, marketplace). 2) Export GeoJSON. 3) De-duplicate with Places results. 4) Verify a sample on the ground or by phone.
Pitfalls to avoid: Incomplete rural coverage in OSM; duplicate entries; outdated places.

Use it for: Scheme rules, equipment costs, recovery rates, season calendar
Tools: Excel/Google Sheets, a 'source' column on every row
Steps: 1) Define the columns first (see Target Schema). 2) One row per fact. 3) Add source, page, date. 4) Have a teammate review a 20% sample.
Pitfalls to avoid: Mixing units; missing sources; undated numbers.

Steps: 1) Write a short template listing capacity and specification. 2) Request 3 quotes per item. 3) Store low/median/high and the quote date. 4) Save screenshots/PDFs.
Pitfalls to avoid: Single quote used as truth; prices excluding GST/installation.

Use it for: Validation benchmark, farmer assumptions, collaboration profiles
Tools: Google Forms, voice notes (with consent), spreadsheet
Steps: 1) Prepare a short question set (see Primary Research). 2) Get consent and explain the purpose. 3) Record answers in a structured sheet. 4) Summarise in the report with sample size.
Pitfalls to avoid: Leading questions; tiny samples presented as proof; storing personal data without consent.

Use it for: Risk indices, distance matrices, tehsil summaries
Steps: 1) Write the formula in code with a docstring. 2) Version the weights. 3) Save the output with the input versions used.

Pitfalls to avoid: Training or validating a model on data generated by the same rules (circular evidence).
